definition: II. מֶ֫שֶׁךְ proper name, of a people the Moschi (Greek Μοσχοι , see below; Assyrian Mušku, Muški , Dl Par 250 E. Schr COT Gen 10:2 ; KGF 155 ff.; compare Sabean משך Hal 243 ); — 'son' of Japheth Gen 10:2 ( P ), between תֻּבָל and תִּירָס , = 1Chr 1:5 also, מֶ֑שֶׁךְ , probably error, v 1Chr 1:17 (see מַשׁ ); מֶ֑שֶׁךְ Ps 120:5 (|| קֵדָר ; here without תֻּבָל ); ׳ תּוּבַל וּמ Ezek 27:13 compare Ezek 32:26 ; Ezek 38:2 (both + תֻּבָל ); so also ᵐ5 Isa 66:19 ( Lo Sta Javan 8 Du Che Hpt ; see above מָשַׁךְ 2. ); וְתֻבָ֑ל ׳ גּוֺג נְשִׂיא ראֹשׁ מ Ezek 38:3 ; Ezek 39:1 . ᵐ5 Μοσοχ ( Μεσοχ ), Samaritan מושׁ(י)ך . — On identification compare Boch.; in Assyrian times they dwelt in west (or northwest) Armenia (compare Schr l.c .); in Persian times apparently farther northeast (southeast of Euxine Sea), compare Μοσχοι καὶ Τιβαρηνοι Herod iii. 94; vii. 78 ; also Di Gen 10:2 and Che Encycl. Blb. Art. Geogr. (Biblical) .
